text: The Jaynes Covered Bridge is a historic covered bridge located in northern Waterville, Vermont, carrying Codding Hollow Road across the North Branch Lamoille River. Constructed around 1877, it is one of three 19th-century covered bridges in Waterville and one of five that span the North Branch Lamoille River within a five-mile stretch. It was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1974. Situated a short distance east of Vermont Route 109 on Codding Hill Road, the bridge is a single-span queen post truss structure measuring 56.5 feet (17.2 m) in length and 15 feet (4.6 m) in width, with a 12-foot (3.7 m) roadway width accommodating one lane. It features a gabled metal roof and vertical board siding that ends before the eaves. The bridge deck has been replaced with steel I-beams covered by wooden planking, meaning the trusses now support only the superstructure, and the joints between the truss posts and diagonals have been reinforced with steel plating. The bridge is one of three period bridges in the town that span the same river, and together with two others in the neighboring town of Belvidere, it represents one of Vermont's highest concentrations of bridges on a single waterway. The builder of the bridge is unknown. Media related to the Jaynes Covered Bridge is available at Wikimedia Commons.
